entries.test: Public financial reports showing the labs' cloud spending, losses, cash requirements and dependence on external funding would test this claim.
entries.note: The surrounding text identifies the two labs as OpenAI and Anthropic.

entries.test: Disclosures of Microsoft, Google and Amazon's capital spending and infrastructure allocations would show whether the overwhelming majority supports OpenAI and Anthropic.
entries.note: Here, hyperscalers refers to the three companies under discussion.
Lacking confidence that a substantial business exists is not equivalent to saying it probably does not exist.

entries.test: Customer concentration disclosures and the labs' financial statements would show their customer rankings and ability to meet cloud bills without continuing external financing.
entries.note: 'Near-infinite' exaggerates an otherwise testable claim of ongoing financing dependence.

entries.test: Azure's FY2026 revenue growth and the year-over-year increase in revenue from OpenAI and Anthropic would establish their share of that growth.
entries.note: FY2026 is supplied by the immediately preceding discussion.

entries.test: Revenue concentration data and investor disclosures would establish the labs' contribution to AI revenues and cloud growth and whether that concentration was disclosed accurately.
entries.note: 'Most' weakens 'vast majority.' Public disclosures can test the allegation without establishing private intent.

entries.test: AI compute orders, utilization and available or committed capacity would show whether demand supports the claim that all that capacity will be used.
entries.note: In context, 'endless, insatiable' concerns demand sufficient to absorb the buildout.
The outcome is explicitly only a potential stall.
The historical superlative expresses a judgment of investment quality without a shared ranking criterion.
'More than likely' expressly qualifies the predicted outcomes.
The conditional conclusion calls spending 'a waste' without defining a financial recovery threshold. Its supporting revenue assertion is also hedged with 'likely.'
The proposition omits the explicit condition that both labs survive and can pay. The spending forecast is qualified by 'likely.'

entries.test: AI revenue breakdowns would establish how much revenue remains after excluding the two labs' compute spending and how dependent the businesses are on that spending.
entries.note: 'Pathetic' is a judgment of adequacy, not precisely a claim that revenues are 'very small.' The dependence assertion has a factual core.

entries.test: Public data on AI customer spending and its financing sources would show whether substantial demand exists independently of hyperscaler funding.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a plain financial meaning for 'paying themselves.'
The proposition strengthens 'doesn't appear' to 'is not.' The revenue estimate is checkable separately, but 'meaningful' and 'questionable value' are evaluative.

entries.test: Paid sales, renewals and customer spending on AI software and AI add-ons would establish whether substantial commercial demand exists.
entries.note: This is a firm assertion about commercial demand.

entries.test: Following either lab's failure, public compute spending and industry output data would show whether at least half disappears and whether the described financing loop ends.
entries.note: He presents this as one of two scenarios. The proposition omits the claimed loss of actual industry production.
He demands new regulations but does not specify the exact regulatory remedy stated in the proposition.

entries.test: If capacity delivery falls behind the schedules underlying projected spending, delivery records and the labs' payments would show whether they can pay for that capacity.
entries.note: The surrounding revenue projections give the condition a practical reference point.

entries.test: If continued infrastructure expansion and lab funding fail, subsequent cloud and associated-service revenue growth would show whether growth slows.
entries.note: 'Stop building' is narrower than failing to build 'more and more.' The proposition also omits associated services.
'Catastrophic failure' judges investment performance without a defined return threshold. Specific underlying financial trends could be checked separately.
This sweeping dismissal does not identify a particular consensus proposition to test.
The proposition removes 'there appears to be.' The claim that the figure overestimates demand is explicitly probabilistic.
The overbuilding assertion is qualified by 'likely.'

entries.test: Disclosed compute commitments, contract schedules and compute use relative to revenue would test whether two $100 billion annual run rates could support the committed demand.
entries.note: This is a hypothetical financial sufficiency comparison using current commitments, rather than a dated forecast. Public quantities can test it.

entries.test: Public financial results and operating plans would show whether either lab has established a financially self-sustaining business model.
entries.note: 'Have not worked out' does not precisely equal having no working business model. The surrounding text frames the issue as financial sustainability.

entries.test: Anthropic's net income for the quarter cited in profitability claims would establish whether it was profitable.
entries.note: His own parenthetical explicitly rejects the reported profitability claim.

entries.test: Public financial statements and disclosed financing plans would establish the labs' losses and whether they have a supported path to operating without continuing external support.
entries.note: 'Infinite resources' is rhetorical emphasis on the financial sustainability claim.
Unprofitability is separately checkable, but 'an impossible rate' supplies no agreed limit or growth trajectory to test.

entries.test: If OpenAI incurs the projected $750 billion compute bill through early 2030, its revenue and financing disclosures would show whether either stated funding threshold was necessary and reached.
entries.note: The proposition omits the 'over the next few years' deadline for raising financing.

entries.test: Public evidence that the strategy collapses or instead becomes durably self-financing while sustaining cloud revenue growth would test the prediction.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph identifies the mission as funding the labs and building capacity to sustain revenue growth.

entries.test: The cited consensus figures and the ratio of $186 billion to $18.7 billion would establish the roughly ten-year payback at a constant revenue level and zero costs.
entries.note: The proposition omits that this is a calculation using a decade of 'those revenues,' holding the estimated annual amount constant.
Near-term survival is explicitly probabilistic. 'Once they do so' also presupposes eventual failure, which could be screened separately.

entries.test: Public data on planned and installed AI data center capacity, utilization and contracted compute demand would show whether capacity exceeds demand.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion establishes capacity relative to commercial compute demand as the comparison.
The proposed disclosure requirement is a recommendation. The allegation about misleading disclosures could be tested separately.

entries.test: Post-cycle financial statements would show whether the companies' balance sheets and financial positions are substantially worse than before the AI investment cycle.
entries.note: The proposition makes Meta's inclusion firm despite 'I guess' and omits the claimed inflation of revenue expectations.
The figures support a judgment that the investment is unjustified; no return horizon or standard of adequacy is specified.

entries.test: Public AI revenue, capital spending and cumulative cash return data would show whether the investments pay back while annual capex remains at least three times AI revenue.
entries.note: The sustained spending condition and financial context give 'pay off' a plain cash-return meaning.
'Air is coming out' and 'deflating' do not specify whether revenue, growth, valuation or financial strength is declining.
The broad conclusion leaves the measure of decline unspecified. 'I believe' alone does not make it a probability claim.

entries.test: Repayment, default and recovery records for the existing AI data center loan pool would establish whether the overwhelming majority goes unpaid and lenders incur losses.
entries.note: 'Most' weakens 'vast majority.' The prediction is firm despite the introductory 'I believe.'

entries.test: Once the asserted demand shortfall becomes publicly established, semiconductor financial reports would show whether revenue or earnings growth falls as predicted.
entries.note: The growth decline is certain and conditional; impairments and restatements are only possibilities. Those possible outcomes are not independently checkable forecasts.

entries.test: If either or both labs fail, public AI industry revenue and compute spending data before and after the failures would establish whether 40% to 73% disappears.
entries.note: The claimed range is explicit and the failure condition is prospective.

entries.test: Comparable AI GPU operating-cost data in August 2031 and August 2026 would establish whether running those GPUs costs as much after five years.
entries.note: The proposition turns an argument against a recovery analogy into a categorical no-recovery prediction and omits the other cost assertions.

entries.test: A failure of either lab and subsequent public evidence of financial damage to dependent companies and lenders would test the predicted collapse and consequences.
entries.note: The text predicts consequences when either explodes; the proposition more strongly says both will collapse.
'Will be the punchline' does not specify who bears which financial losses. The proposition gives the metaphor a more specific financial commitment.
